_meta.project: instex Instrument Explorer -- IMAGER mode preset: Palomar 200-inch Hale / 4-Shooter (pyramid-split four-camera reimaging CCD imager at the Cassegrain focus)
_meta.companion: data/imaging/fourshooter.md (same content as Markdown). Structure follows data/imaging/widefield.json: sources{key: cite, file, url}; instrument entry: title, preset (machine-readable explorer inputs), recommended_preset (prose), params, performance (validation targets), not_found, conflicts, notes.
_meta.model: Cassegrain focus (D, F_tel) -> four-faceted reflecting pyramid at the focal plane -> per quadrant: ideal collimator f_col (= F_tel x W) -> pupil of diameter W -> ideal camera f_cam -> CCD. Effective focal ratio = f_cam / W; pixel scale = 206265 x p / (D x F_tel x f_cam / f_col).
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/imaging/fourshooter/ (OG82 and PDS: existing rawdata/presets/longslit_dbsp/ files). derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). value null = NOT FOUND; nothing is filled from memory.
_meta.quote_normalisation: Unicode NFKC; curly quotes, primes, dashes, minus, multiplication and tilde signs mapped to ASCII; whitespace collapsed; a piece also passes after joining hyphenated line breaks ('-' + whitespace removed) or with all whitespace removed; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces. OCR glyph errors in the source text are kept verbatim inside the quotes.
_meta.quote_check: Machine-checked by script against: pdftotext -layout and -raw (the ADS scans' text layers are OCR); tesseract 5.5.1 OCR of the page images for P84, G84 and B61 (no text layer) and for CPM86 pp. 348-349 and S86 p. 992; tag-stripped and raw HTML for PHT and PDS; the decoded ADS API record for G87OE.

detector.name: Texas Instruments 800 x 800 (WF/PC type)
detector.layout: 2 x 2 contiguous on the sky, one chip per pyramid facet; chips physically separate in their own housings

fourshooter.recommended_preset: D = 5.08 m (200-in primary, B61; '5.1 m', PHT), eps = 0.36 DERIVED (72-in prime-focus cage, which carries the Cassegrain secondary, / 200 in; the 40-in hole is inside its shadow), Cassegrain f/16 (P84, B61, PHT; f = 81,280 mm DERIVED from 3200 in; 2.538"/mm), primary f/3.3 (drawing only). Splitter: a four-faceted reflecting pyramid coincident with the Cassegrain focal plane (S94, P96, P84), the WF/PC focal-plane image splitter design (G84); light meets the facets at ~5 deg incidence (Z87), so each quadrant is sent back up ~10 deg off axis (DERIVED) to its own reimager. Each reimager: collimated beam (CPM86) -> 4-in filter in one of two wheels ~1 m above the pyramid (S94) -> small Schmidt camera (P84) at f/1.8 (P84; f/1.818 DERIVED from 0.335"/px), i.e. f_cam/f_col = 0.1136 DERIVED; f_col, W and f_cam are NOT published. Detectors: four TI 800 x 800 CCDs, 15 um (CPM86), 2 x 2 contiguous on the sky (chip 1 NE, 4 NW, 2 SE, 3 SW; readout columns parallel), no sky gap by design but a ~1" unusable crack along the facet edges (C86; 'few arcsec', P96) and 20 dark px along the two apex edges of each chip (S94, P96). Validate: 0.335"/px (P84 Table I, S94, D92, N95), field 8'56" x 8'56" = 1600 x 1600 px (P84; 8.9', S94/P96), 4.4' per camera (CPM86).

pyramid_angle.unit: deg (angle of incidence on the pyramid facets)
pyramid_angle.quote: The angle of incidence at this mirror is about 5°, ... leading to an instrumental polarization of ^0.8%.
pyramid_angle.note: Only published geometric angle. The facet tilt, facet size and apex height are NOT published.
pyramid_angle.derived: DERIVED (geometry, assuming the quoted incidence is that of the beam centre arriving along the telescope axis): each facet is tilted ~5 deg from the plane normal to the axis (a very flat pyramid), and each reflected beam leaves ~2 x 5 = 10 deg from the reversed telescope axis, i.e. back up toward the primary; at 1 m from the pyramid its axis is ~176 mm off the telescope axis (1000 x tan 10 deg), well clear of the incoming f/16 cone (half-angle atan(1/32) = 1.8 deg; radius 31 mm at 1 m plus the field). Facet orientation: the quadrant boundaries form a cross (S94 Fig. 1), so with plane facets the four pyramid edges lie along that cross and each facet's tilt is along a field diagonal; the four beams then leave toward the four corners of the field. This follows from geometry, not from a source.

camera_reduction.derived: DERIVED: (206264.8 x 0.015 / 0.335) / 81280 = 9236 / 81280 = 0.1136, i.e. a 8.80x reduction of the f/16 image (f/16 -> f/1.818). From the two published f-ratios alone: 1.8 / 16 = 0.1125 (8.89x).

Order-of-magnitude bound only (DERIVED, not a design value): the filters sit in the collimated beam (CPM86) 'about a meter above the pyramid' (S94), so the collimator is roughly <= 1 m from the f/16 focus, f_col <~ 1000 mm and W = f_col / 16 <~ 62 mm. not_found: The 4-Shooter instrument paper itself (Gunn et al. 1987, Optical Engineering 26, 779 = G87OE): only the ADS abstract was obtained (SPIE blocked the download). PASP 99, 518 (Gunn, Emory, Harris & Oke 1987) is the Palomar Dewar + CCD-electronics paper, not the 4-Shooter optics paper; it cites G87OE for the 4-Shooter.

Imaging-channel optics: collimator type and focal length, collimated-beam (pupil) diameter W and its position, Schmidt-camera focal length and aperture. Only f/1.8 at the CCD (P84) and the 0.335"/px scale are published; f_cam/f_col = 0.1136 is DERIVED. The explorer needs W only for the drawing (order-of-magnitude bound W <~ 62 mm, DERIVED, see collimator_and_pupil).

Pyramid figure and dimensions: facet shape (P84 says the pyramid 'flattens the field', so possibly curved), facet tilt (only the ~5 deg angle of incidence, Z87), physical size (~211 mm square DERIVED from the field), and the direction in which each beam leaves (diagonal routing DERIVED from geometry).
A 4-Shooter-era central obscuration: only the 72-in prime-focus cage of the 1961 description (B61) -> eps = 0.36 DERIVED; spider-vane widths not found.
Physical gap between chips: irrelevant optically (each chip has its own camera); the chips sit in separate housings (P84) and are 'physically well separated' (Z87).
Later upgrades (other CCDs, new cameras) and the decommissioning date: none found in the saved sources; every description from 1984 to 1996 has four TI 800 x 800 CCDs at ~0.335"/px.
conflicts: Primary source: the brief cites Gunn et al. 1987, PASP 99, 518 as the 4-Shooter paper; that paper is 'The Palomar Observatory CCD camera' (Gunn, Emory, Harris & Oke; Dewars and electronics) and cites 'Gunn, J. E., et al. 1987, Optical Engineering, in press' for the 4-Shooter -> Opt. Eng. 26, 779 (G87OE).

Cassegrain f-ratio: f/16 (P84; B61 3200-in focal length; PHT 81.3 m) vs f/15.7 (OG82) vs f/15.80 DERIVED from the DBSP slit scale 2.57"/mm (PDS); OG82's own '2.5 arc sec mm-1' implies f/16.24 (DERIVED).

Pixel scale: 0.335" (P84 Table I, S94, D92, N95; P96 'approximately') vs 0.336" (S85, first data) vs 0.334" nominal (CPM86) vs 0.33" (G87OE abstract, Z87, rounded); f/1.8 (P84) would give 0.338" (DERIVED).

Field: 8'56" x 8'56" (P84 Table I; = 1600 x 0.335" DERIVED) vs 8.9' (S94, P96) vs 9' x 9' (P84 text, N95, Z87) vs ~8.5' (G84, first announcement) vs ~60 arcmin^2 (N95; the 1600-px square is 79.8 arcmin^2 DERIVED, 75.9 arcmin^2 with the 20-px shadowed edges removed); usable scan width 520" (P96) or 496" (S94 grism survey).

Dead zone between quadrants: ~1" crack (C86) vs 'the few arcseconds of sky ... not usable' (P96) vs a ~4" strip without objects in the grism survey (S94); no gap by design, with 20 px per chip edge unexposed (S94, P96).
Per-chip format: 800 x 800 (P84, S94, P96, N95, G84) vs 800 x 816 read out (Z87; the extra 16 columns are probably the extended-register overscan, S94; interpretation).
Installation: 1983 (P96) vs mounted 'this spring' of 1984 (P84, tests March 1984; S85 first data 1984 June).
System efficiency: nearly 50% at peak incl. telescope (G87OE) vs ~40% (G84) vs 30% in the red (P84, 1984 measurement).
notes: Explorer mapping (pyramid splitter): telescope Cassegrain, D = 5.08 m, eps = 0.36, F = 16 (f = 81,280 mm), primary f/3.3. Pyramid at the f/16 focal plane, four facets, one per field quadrant, angle of incidence ~5 deg -> each quadrant reflected back up ~10 deg off axis (DERIVED) into its own reimager: collimator (f_col, W not published) -> filter (4-in, collimated beam) -> small Schmidt camera (f/1.8 published; f/1.818 DERIVED) -> TI 800 x 800, 15 um CCD. Each chip sees 4.47' (800 px x 0.335"); the four sky quadrants abut in a 2 x 2 square 8.93' on a side with a ~1" unusable crack along the cross; 20 px along the two apex edges of each chip are dark (pyramid shadow).

Drawing placeholder (NOT a published design value): f_col = 1000 mm (the 'about a meter' pyramid-to-filter distance, S94) -> W = 1000 / 16 = 62.5 mm, f_cam = 0.1136 x 1000 = 113.6 mm (f_cam / W = 1.818); only the ratio f_cam / f_col affects the pixel scale.

Heritage: the splitter is the focal-plane image splitter developed for Hubble's Wide Field/Planetary Camera (G84, CPM86), and the CCDs are the TI chips built for WF/PC (P84); the predecessor was Gunn & Westphal's prime-focus PFUEI (P84: the 4-Shooter's 'simpler optical system with better coatings' vs PFUEI's 22 glass/air surfaces).

Other modes: an auxiliary long-slit spectrograph behind a slit cut into one pyramid facet (S86: 1.5" x 2.0', Cassegrain Schmidt camera f/1.33 in a 3-in beam, 0.426"/px; the slit shows as a diagonal line in direct images, S91), simultaneous imaging on the other quadrants (S86), slitless grisms in front of all four CCDs, and drift-scan (transit) imaging with the CCD columns aligned east-west, triple-clocked (S94; G87OE 'scanning mode').
Preset configuration: the direct-imaging Cassegrain 4-Shooter as described 1984-1996 (no later upgrade found). Unbinned 0.335"/px; N95 resampled 3 x 3 px into 2 x 2 (0.502"/px) for its catalogs.

Quote-check caveats: all journal sources are ADS page scans; their text layers are OCR and carry glyph errors that are kept verbatim in the quotes (e.g. '0"334' = 0.334", 'fxm'/'wu' = um, '//15.7' = f/15.7, '^' = ~, 'Â' = Angstrom). The three scans without a text layer (P84, G84, B61) and the pages CPM86 pp. 348-349 and S86 p. 992 were OCR'd here with tesseract 5.5.1.
